title: Dense-subgroup fixed ideals and rational finite jets
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field] [def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $G$ be a smooth affine finite-type $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $\Gamma\subseteq G(k)$ be an abstract subgroup Zariski dense in $|G|$. Let $X$ be an affine finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme] with a $G$-action, meaning a morphism $G\times_kX\to X$ satisfying the identity and associativity laws [def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose a closed immersion $F\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] represents, on every commutative $k$-algebra $R$, the subfunctor of $x\in X(R)$ fixed by every $\gamma_R$, $\gamma\in\Gamma$. Fix $x\in F(k)$. Then $x$ is fixed by $G$ scheme-theoretically: for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$ and $g\in G(R)$, $g x_R=x_R$. Put $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and let $\mathfrak m$ be its maximal ideal, with residue field $k$. For $\gamma\in\Gamma$, write $\gamma^*$ for pullback on $A$ along the automorphism $z\mapsto\gamma^{-1}z$, and put $J=(\gamma^*f-f\mid\gamma\in\Gamma,\ f\in\mathfrak m)$. The immersion induces an isomorphism $\mathcal O_{F,x}\cong A/J$ of local $k$-algebras. For every integer $n\geq1$, $A/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$ is a finite-dimensional rational $G$-algebra: it has an algebra coaction into $(A/\mathfrak m^{n+1})\otimes_k k[G]$ satisfying coassociativity and the counit identity, whose evaluation at $\gamma$ induces $\gamma^*$. Here $k[G]$ is the coordinate ring of the affine scheme $G$. The subspace $M_n=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$ is a rational $G$-subrepresentation, $V=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ has the induced rational representation, and the quotient $q_n:M_n\twoheadrightarrow V$ is $G$-equivariant. A rational linear representation means a linear coaction satisfying those identities, equivalently a group-scheme homomorphism to $\operatorname{GL}(W)$, where $\operatorname{GL}(W)(R)=\operatorname{Aut}_R(W\otimes_k R)$. Neither smoothness of $X$ nor linear reductivity of $G$ is assumed.

source.place: Propositions 1.10 and 1.13, printed pp.9--10 (dense-point detection); Lemma 13.4, printed p.255 (local difference ideal); proof of Lemma 13.6, printed p.256 (finite jets), with the algebraic-action construction of Section 4(d), printed pp.86--87, and the fixed-point argument in the proof of Proposition 8.9. Inverse pullbacks give a left representation; the ideal is unchanged because Gamma is a group.

proof.text: Write $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $G=\operatorname{Spec}C$, with $C=k[G]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Both coordinate algebras are finitely generated by [lem-pc-affine-finite-type-algebra]. Smoothness of $G\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ gives reducedness of its sole fibre $G$ by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], and thus $C$ is reduced by [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. We will use the following direct consequence of [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq]: if $h\in C$ vanishes at every $\gamma\in\Gamma$, the closed set $V((h))$ contains the dense set $\Gamma$, hence is all of $\operatorname{Spec}C=V(0)$. The cited radical equality gives $h\in\sqrt{(h)}=\sqrt0$, so $h=0$. This is density in all components; connectedness is not used.

source.place: Proposition 1.10, printed pp.9--10; the scalar dense-point test. Stacks 056T (varieties-lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal) via the cited smooth-fibre node, and 00E0 (algebra-lemma-Zariski-topology), (6)--(7), via the cited radical node.

proof.text: Use the right action $(z,g)\mapsto g^{-1}z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and [def-weil-affine-spectrum], its pullback is an algebra map $c:B\to B\otimes_kC$, with the algebra tensor structure of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Let $\Delta,\epsilon$ be the multiplication and identity pullbacks of $C$ from [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf]. Pullback of $(z\cdot g)\cdot h=z\cdot(gh)$ and $z\cdot e=z$ gives $(c\otimes1)c=(1\otimes\Delta)c$ and $(1\otimes\epsilon)c=1$. Here tensor associativity and symmetry send pure tensors to the corresponding reordered tensors, using [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Evaluation of $c$ at $g\in G(R)$ is pullback by $z\mapsto g^{-1}z$ on $X_R$. In particular evaluation at $\gamma$ is the stipulated $\gamma^*$ on $B$.

source.place: Section 4(d), printed pp.86--87: right actions on affine schemes give coordinate comodules; inverse pullbacks turn the given left action into this right action.

proof.text: Write $x:B\to k$ for the given point. For every $b\in B$, the function $h_b=(x\otimes1)c(b)-x(b)1_C$ vanishes at $\gamma\in\Gamma$: $x$ is fixed by $\gamma^{-1}$, since $\Gamma$ is a group. Step 1 gives $h_b=0$. Evaluating this identity along any $k$-algebra map $g:C\to R$ gives $b(g^{-1}x_R)=b(x_R)$ for every $b$, using the tensor algebra evaluation map in [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. The affine point correspondence [def-weil-affine-spectrum] therefore gives $g^{-1}x_R=x_R$. Replace $g$ by $g^{-1}$ to get the required scheme-theoretic fixedness for every $R$, including nonreduced $R$.

source.place: Propositions 1.10 and 1.13, printed pp.9--10; fixed-point argument preceding Lemma 13.6, printed p.256, written in coordinates.

proof.text: Let $I=(\gamma^*b-b\mid\gamma\in\Gamma,b\in B)$. A $k$-algebra map $q:B\to R$ kills $I$ exactly when $q\gamma^*=q$ for all $\gamma$, that is, its point is fixed by every $\gamma_R^{-1}$, equivalently every $\gamma_R$. Write $F=\operatorname{Spec}(B/K)$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The two quotient maps $B\to B/I$ and $B\to B/K$ belong to the same prescribed fixed subfunctor, so the first kills $K$ and the second kills $I$. Thus $K\subseteq I$ and $I\subseteq K$. Consequently $K=I$, as actual ideals, by the quotient kernel description [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. No radical or reducedness assertion about $F$ is involved.

source.place: Lemma 13.4 and preceding fixed-subfunctor paragraph, printed p.255, affine algebra-valued-point proof.

proof.text:
Put $\mathfrak p=\ker(x:B\to k)$. The point is rational, so $B/\mathfrak p=k$, and fixedness gives $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$ and $\gamma^*\mathfrak p=\mathfrak p$ (use $\gamma^{-1}$ for the reverse inclusion). By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-stalk-localization] and [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $A=B_{\mathfrak p}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pA$, and $\gamma^*(b/s)=\gamma^*b/\gamma^*s$. Each generator $\gamma^*b-b$ of $I$ is the difference of $b-x(b)\in\mathfrak p$, giving $IA\subseteq J$. Conversely,
$$\gamma^*(b/s)-b/s=\frac{s(\gamma^*b-b)-b(\gamma^*s-s)}{s\gamma^*s}\in IA.$$
The denominator avoids $\mathfrak p$. Thus $J=IA$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient] to $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$ and the point $\mathfrak p/I$ of $F$; its fraction formula identifies the immersion's stalk map with $A\to A/IA$. This proves $\mathcal O_{F,x}\cong A/J$ as local $k$-algebras.

source.place: Lemma 13.4, printed p.255; localization and difference calculation supplied explicitly, with the cited stalk and quotient-localization statements.

proof.text:
For $N\geq2$ put $D_N=B/\mathfrak p^N$. Choose finitely many algebra generators $b_1,\ldots,b_e$ of $B$ by [lem-pc-affine-finite-type-algebra], and set $y_i=b_i-x(b_i)$. Expansion of a polynomial around the scalars $x(b_i)$ shows that $\mathfrak p=(y_1,\ldots,y_e)$. Hence $D_N$ is spanned by the finitely many monomials in the $y_i$ of total degree $<N$, and is finite-dimensional in the sense of [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]. For $s
otin\mathfrak p$, its image is $x(s)+v$, with $x(s)
e0$ and $v^N=0$, so its inverse is
$$x(s)^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}(-v/x(s))^j.$$
The formula $b/s\mapsto ar b ar s^{-1}$ therefore defines $A	o D_N$: a fraction relation $u(bs'-b's)=0$ becomes equality after multiplication by the inverse of $ ar u ar s ar s'$. It kills $\mathfrak m^N$. Its induced map $A/\mathfrak m^N	o D_N$ and the map $D_N	o A/\mathfrak m^N$ induced by $B	o A$ are inverse, since they fix $B$ and the inverses of every $s
otin\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. These identifications respect the augmentation to $k$ and the reductions for different $N$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 8.9, printed p.150, finite local neighbourhoods; proof of Lemma 13.6, printed p.256. Polynomial expansion and nilpotent inverse provide the affine calculation without smoothness of X.

proof.text:
Step 3 says $(x\otimes1)c(b)=x(b)1_C$. The splitting $B=k\cdot1\oplus\mathfrak p$, given by $b=x(b)1+(b-x(b))$, gives
$$\ker(x\otimes1:B\otimes_kC\to C)=\mathfrak p\otimes_kC.$$
Indeed the maps induced by the projection $b\mapsto b-x(b)$ and the inclusion of $\mathfrak p$ give this direct sum decomposition after tensoring [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Thus $c(\mathfrak p)\subseteq\mathfrak p\otimes_kC$. Since $c$ is multiplicative, $c(\mathfrak p^N)$ is a sum of tensors whose first factors lie in $\mathfrak p^N$. The algebra map $(q_N\otimes1)c$ therefore kills $\mathfrak p^N$ and defines $c_N:D_N\to D_N\otimes_kC$ by $c_N(\bar b)=(q_N\otimes1)c(b)$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient, lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Applying $q_N$ to the first factor of the two identities in Step 2 proves coassociativity and the counit identity for $c_N$; equality on $D_N$ follows by lifting each $\bar b$ to $B$. Transport this algebra coaction through Step 6 to $A/\mathfrak m^N$.

source.place: Section 4(d), printed pp.86--87; proof of Lemma 13.6, printed p.256. Augmentation splitting and descent to finite jets written explicitly.

proof.text: The same formula for $c_N$ sends $\mathfrak p/\mathfrak p^N$ into $(\mathfrak p/\mathfrak p^N)\otimes_kC$, because $c(\mathfrak p)\subseteq\mathfrak p\otimes_kC$. This tensor inclusion is faithful: split $D_N=k\oplus(\mathfrak p/\mathfrak p^N)$ by its augmentation, as in Step 7 [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The restriction is consequently a linear coaction. Reduction $D_N\to D_2$ commutes with coactions, since both composites send $\bar b$ to the reduction of $c(b)$ modulo $\mathfrak p^2$ in its first factor. The restricted map $\mathfrak p/\mathfrak p^N\to\mathfrak p/\mathfrak p^2$ is onto by lifting a class to $\mathfrak p$. Step 6 identifies it with $q_n:M_n\to V$ when $N=n+1$. For $n=1$ it is the identity. Evaluation of $c_N$ at $\gamma$ agrees with $\gamma^*$ on the image of $B$; it agrees on every fraction because an algebra homomorphism sends the inverse of $s$ to the unique inverse of its image. Thus these are exactly the local actions required by the statement.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 13.6, printed p.256, the finite-jet representations and their map to the cotangent space; compatible quotient formula supplied explicitly.

proof.text: The finite-dimensional coactions of Steps 7--8 give rational $G$-representations by [lem-sfb-rational-representation-comodule-dictionary]. Its finite-dimensional clause identifies these with group-scheme homomorphisms to $\operatorname{GL}$, and its intertwining clause gives equivariance of $q_n$. The action on $D_N$ is by algebra maps because $c_N$ is an algebra map; the inverse of the action of $g$ is the action of $g^{-1}$ by the same dictionary. The restricted spaces are finite-dimensional: any subspace of the span of finitely many monomials in Step 6 has a basis of at most that many elements (successively retain a vector only when independent). This proves all rational algebra and subrepresentation assertions. No step used regularity of $A$, smoothness of $X$, or complete reducibility.
